title: Single-cell modeling identifies a BRCA-enriched fallopian secretory-cell state
summary: A University of Cambridge-led preprint uses MetaCell clustering to analyze 168,679 fallopian-tube cells from 34 women, including 15 BRCA1/2 carriers, and identifies secretory-cell states enriched among carriers with high TP53 and histone expression. A trained QuPath image classifier also supports the spatial p53 analysis; matched protein measurements found increased DNA-damage markers in selected samples. These findings support a bounded replication-stress association, without establishing prospective cancer prediction or causal malignant transformation. This represents the August 27, 2026 first preprint; a November 22 revision is the same study.
ai_technology: MetaCell unsupervised graph-based single-cell clustering; QuPath trained cell-type image classifier
organization: University of Cambridge; University College London; Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust; Francis Crick Institute; University of British Columbia

evidence.tested: Single-cell transcriptional analysis of 55 samples from 34 women, including 15 BRCA1/2 carriers, plus within-study p53 immunohistochemistry and matched multiplex protein-marker measurements.
evidence.unknown: The study does not establish prospective cancer-risk prediction, causal transformation or clinical utility. Protein validation uses a subset of slides, and the cohort is modest; all figures and associations are source-reported.
evidence.ai_role: MetaCell estimates homogeneous transcriptional states from noisy single-cell data, helping reveal rare secretory-cell subpopulations. Separately, QuPath uses a classifier trained on annotated epithelial, stromal and red-blood/debris examples to assign cell types for spatial p53 analysis.
